title: mUnit lint rules
description: A rule file for munit lint: one rule, a list of rules, or { "rules": [...] }. Each rule is a JSON object whose "kind" picks what is checked. The reference is lint-rules/README.md in the mUnit package.

$schema.description: The schema of this file, for editor completion: "./rule.schema.json" relative to this file.

rule.description: One rule. "kind" picks what is checked; the rest parameterises it.

level.description: What a finding does: "warn" is reported, "block" is reported and makes `munit lint` exit 1 (fails CI), "off" turns the rule off. Default "warn".

match.description: Which boxes the rule looks at. Every field given must match.

object.description: Object name(s). Names are normalised like the box's: "t", "trigger", "zl reg" and "zl.reg" all work, and UI objects match by their class ("toggle"). Several names match any of them.

args.description: Positional argument patterns, matched from the first argument; "*" matches any one argument. The box may have more arguments than patterns.

text.description: A regular expression over the whole box text, e.g. "^print$" for a [print] with no name.

scope.description: Which patchers in a file the rule looks at, by namespace. Default ["box"].

namespace.description: "box" (an ordinary patcher), "dsp.gen" ([gen~] and .gendsp), "jit.gen" ([jit.gen], [jit.pix], [jit.gl.pix]), "rnbo" ([rnbo~] and .rnbopat), or "*" for all of them.

forbid-object.title: forbid-object
forbid-object.description: A matching box is not allowed.

forbid-path.title: forbid-path
forbid-path.description: A path of cords from a box matching "from" reaches a box matching "to" without passing a box matching "unless". Cords are followed through every outlet within one patcher; the source box is reported, with the path.

fanout-without-trigger.title: fanout-without-trigger
fanout-without-trigger.description: One message outlet connected to several inlets, so the order of the messages depends on the layout. Signal outlets are exempt. Put a [trigger] between them.

overlapping-boxes.title: overlapping-boxes
overlapping-boxes.description: Two boxes in a patcher overlap in patching view, so one hides the other. The box drawn on top (later in the file) is reported. Boxes sent to the background (@background 1) are exempt.

target.description: "varname": the scripting name of any box; "send": [send], [send~], [mc.send~], [forward]; "receive": [receive], [receive~], [mc.receive~]; "send-receive": both. [value], [pv] and [pvar] count as both.

script.title: script
